# `adi-relay` — types

> Client half of the webhook relay (ADI-MONO-220/222/227): a node's own ed25519 signing key and X25519 sealing key, request signing against the relay's wire contract, sealed-box open/seal, OpenSSH rendering/parsing of the public signing key, and the register/deregister HTTP calls a trigger save or delete makes (register module). Used by adi-app (the poller, the panel's save) and adi-cli (the node side, ADI-MONO-223, and `triggers save`'s own save) as well as by adi-relay-server (verification and sealing, never a node's own keys or the register module's HTTP calls).

## `src/keys.rs`

### struct `RelayIdentity`

This node's two relay keys, loaded together because every relay-backed trigger on the node shares the one pair: one pair per node, not per trigger — the relay tells triggers apart by `endpoint_id`, not by key.

```rust
pub struct RelayIdentity {
    pub signing: SigningKey,
    pub sealing: StaticSecret,
}
```

## `src/openssh.rs`

### enum `ParseError`

Everything that can go wrong turning a line of text back into a key.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum ParseError {
    Empty,
    WrongType(String),
    BadBase64,
    Truncated,
    BadLength(usize),
    BadPoint(SignatureError),
}
```

### struct `Fingerprint`

A stable identifier for a public key, independent of how many times it's transmitted: sha256 of the OpenSSH line's `type base64` prefix (never a trailing comment, which isn't part of the key), hex-encoded. This is `endpoints.owner_fingerprint` in the relay's schema and the value every nonce row is scoped by.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Fingerprint(String);
```

## `src/register.rs`

### struct `Registered`

What `register` persists into the trigger's own `extra`. `url` (`register`'s own echo of the public sender-facing URL) isn't kept here — see `public_url`, which reconstructs it the same way the relay built it, from `relay` + `relay_endpoint`, so there's no fourth `extra` key for it — only `relay`, `relay_retention`, and `relay_endpoint`.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Registered {
    pub endpoint_id: String,
}
```

### enum `Cleanup`

How `register_on_save` should run a best-effort relay delete — the two shapes its two real callers need, and the reason there are two: a bare `tokio::spawn` of an async block that is never awaited is **not** reliably seen through by a `tokio::Runtime` dropped right after, as the obvious fix once looked like it should be — confirmed by hand (a task spawned just before `block_on` returns, sleeping 200ms, left no trace of having run at all once the temporary `Runtime` `Builder::new_multi_thread()...build()` produces was dropped). A `Runtime::drop` only waits out tasks already making progress on a worker, not one that never got polled.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Cleanup {
    Spawn,
    Await,
}
```

### enum `Plan`

Whether, and how, a save needs to touch the relay before anything is persisted. Operates on the manifest's `extra` map directly (not `adi_triggers::Trigger`/`TriggerManifest`) so this crate never has to depend on the trigger-store crate for it.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Plan {
    Unchanged,
    Register {
        url: String,
    },
    Deregister {
        url: String,
        endpoint_id: String,
    },
}
```

## `src/seal.rs`

### struct `Sealed`

One sealed record, exactly the three fields the pull response's wire contract carries and the relay's own schema stores — base64 on the wire, raw bytes here; the caller decides which it needs.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Sealed {
    pub ephemeral_pubkey: [u8; 32],
    pub nonce: [u8; 24],
    pub ciphertext: Vec<u8>,
}
```

### struct `OpenError`

Everything that can go wrong opening a sealed record — deliberately one variant: every cause (wrong AAD, tampered ciphertext, a `sealing_secret` that doesn't match the key the record was sealed to) looks the same to a caller and none should be diagnosable from the outside, the same stance `lease_seal::open` takes.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct OpenError;
```

## `src/sign.rs`

### struct `SignedRequest`

One signed request's worth of header values, read off or about to be written onto the wire — `key_line` is the full `X-Relay-Key` value, not a fingerprint: the full public key rides on every request, since the signature has to be self-contained.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SignedRequest {
    pub key_line: String,
    pub timestamp: u64,
    pub nonce: String,
    pub signature: String,
}
```

### enum `VerifyError`

Everything that can go wrong verifying a signed request — deliberately distinguished (unlike `crate::seal::OpenError`'s single "didn't open"), because the relay's own error codes are stated per failure: `bad_signature` covers everything here except a timestamp outside the skew window, which the caller checks separately with `within_skew` before ever reaching this function, since that's cheaper to reject.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum VerifyError {
    BadKeyLine(ParseError),
    BadSignatureEncoding,
    BadSignature,
}
```
